chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, all of them, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the obligatory share of the grandfather, so he said: 'I do not know anyone among the people who has a ruling for it except by personal opinion, except for Ali (peace be upon him), for he ruled in it with the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zurara,
from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), similar to it.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir, peace be upon him)
key_terms.فَرِيضَةُ الْجَدِّ: The obligatory share of the grandfather in inheritance

ai.seo_question: What is the basis for the grandfather's inheritance share according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the jurisprudential distinction between the Ahl al-Bayt's reliance on prophetic tradition and the general scholarly reliance on personal reasoning (ra'y) regarding the grandfather's inheritance share. It underscores the unique authority of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) in preserving the precise legal rulings of the Prophet, a key theme in Shia usul al-fiqh. The narration serves as a critical reference for determining whether the grandfather inherits as a residuary heir or alongside other relatives.
